etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 御(お) (o-) + 願(ねが)う (negau, “request, implore”) + します (shimasu, a polite honorific (丁(てい)寧(ねい)語(ご) (teineigo)) formula used to show respect to the hearer). The latter portion is the formal or socially distanced form of する (suru). See also ます (-masu, suffix).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compare さして (sashite, “(not) to such an extent”), from 然(さ) (sa), and さして (sashite, conjunctive form of さす (sasu)). For the latter, note readings さす (sasu) of kanji 扨 and 扠, also alternative spellings of this term.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 積(つ)もる (tsumoru, “to intend”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: に (ni, “to”, a particle which modifies the previous word) + ついて (tsuite, -te conjunctive form of the verb 就く (tsuku))

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Derivation unknown. First attested in 1477, around the Muromachi Period.
Historical kana orthography shows that this was originally まう (mau), and Portuguese sources from the late 1500s and early 1600s record this as ⟨mǒ⟩, indicating a pronunciation of /mɔː/ as part of the regular sound shift from /au/ to /oː/.
The initial ma is speculatively connected to 今 (ima, “now”) (compare both the loss of initial i- in 未だ (imada > mada) or 出る (ideru > deru) and the similar -a → -ō shift seen in emphatic particle のう (nō)). Frellesvig suggests a shift from a topicalized form /ima wa/ → /mau/ → /mɔː/ → /moː/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 久しい (hisashii, “long”, (of time)) + 振り (-buri, “first time after”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 乗り (nori, “getting on, riding”, from verb 乗る noru “to ride, to be on top of”) + 換える (kaeru, “to exchange, to change”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Doublet of 窺(うかが)う (ukagau, “to peek”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 全國 (MC dzjwen kwok, literally “whole country”).
First attested in the mid-1800s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kwen/ → /ken/
From Middle Chinese 券 (MC khjwonH, “ticket”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 劇(げき) (geki, “drama”) + 場(じょう) (jō, “place”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese ます (“to increase”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, first appearing in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE with the phonetic spelling 須彌 ⟨sumi₁⟩. Cognate with 炭 (sumi, “charcoal”).
In turn, from Proto-Japonic *sumi. Cognate with Southern Amami Ōshima 墨 (sïmi).
Possibly derived from the homophonous 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) 済み (sumi) of verb 済む (sumu, “to finish, to conclude”), from the way that cinders are left after a fire has finished burning.
Possibly also related to 煤 (susu, “soot”), from which India ink is made.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 大陸／大陆 (dàlù).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese; attested in the Ryūnoshūge (738) as 売比 ⟨me₁ pi₁⟩.
* ⟨me₁ pi₁⟩ → /mefi/ → /mei/
The initial me- has been frequently associated with 女 (me, “female”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Literally ‘inside the house’ from the Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) readings of
家 (ka, “house”)
+ 内 (nai, “inside”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 心 (shin, “heart”) + 身 (shin, “body”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 我 (ware, “I; me”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Doublet of 彫(ほ)る (horu, “to carve”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 最 (sai-, “most”) + 高 (kō, “high”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 欠 is a daiyōji replacing 缺.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Transitive verb derived from 直(なお) (nao, “straight; common, normal, ordinary”) + transitive / causative suffixing element す (su). Cognate with 治(なお)す (naosu, “to cure, to heal”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 肌(はだ) (hada, “skin”) + 着(ぎ) (-gi, “clothing”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 豪華 (MC haw hwae|xwae|hwaeH, literally “grand + flowery”). Compare modern Cantonese reading hou⁴ waa⁴.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 近 (“near”) + 代 (“age; period”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *op- ~ əp-. Perhaps cognate with 負う (ou, “to carry on the back”), as both words involve the movement of one person behind another person, but the accent values in Early Middle Japanese and Kyoto do not match.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. Derived from older form 閉(と)づ (tozu) via regular historical processes in the shift to the 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) pattern. Over time, the distinction between ぢ (dji) and じ (ji) was lost, leading to the modern spelling of とじる (tojiru).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 上(かみ)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami nidan katsuyō, “upper bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 上(かみ)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 閉づ entry.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 限(かぎ)る (kagiru, “to limit, to restrict”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 黄 (ki, “yellow”) + 色 (iro, “colour”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 黄色 (ɦwɑŋ ʃɨk̚).
